text: The following resolution rule is used in logic programming. Derive clause (P ∨ Q) from clauses (P ∨ R), (Q ∨ ¬R). Which of the following statements related to this rule is FALSE?
options: (P ∨ Q) is satisfiable if and only if (P ∨ R) ∧ (Q ∨ ¬R) is satisfiable
(P ∨ Q) ⇒ FALSE if and only if both P and Q are unsatisfiable
solution: (A) is exactly the resolution rule and simplifies to 1, so it is valid. (B) simplifies to (¬P∧¬Q) ∨ (P∧Q) ∨ (P∧¬R) ∨ (Q∧R), a contingency, so it is not logically valid - hence the FALSE statement. (C) and (D) both hold.
source_label: GATE Overflow question page - GATE CSE 2003 Q.72 with community solutions
answer_evidence: which is a contingency $($can be TRUE or FALSE depending on values of $P,Q$ and $R)$ and hence not logically valid. Answer B.
